reviewedSecretBehavior: The only runtime writer call uses self.pg_env[POSTGRES_PASSWORD], generated inside the fixture constructor with secrets.token_urlsafe(32). Its CLI takes image/revision/context/output selection, not deployment or user credentials. Test-only callers use synthetic literals or the same generated fixture value; the local original alias is confined to an interruption/cleanup test.

Native Linux/amd64 host/daemon admission and an actual writable host tmpfs precede runtime directory creation. Descriptor-held nofollow ancestor checks, private 0700 owner directory, exclusive single-link 0600 leaf, literal plaintext write, flush, 0444 mode and post-close identity checks are unchanged.

Failure cleanup retains descriptor ownership and unlinks only the witnessed original inode; ordinary completion cleans the private temporary directory after owned fixture resource cleanup. Existing Docker environment filtering and diagnostic redaction are unchanged.

The added request is a GET to the literal /public/static/altcha.umd.js on 127.0.0.1:9000 inside the owned runtime. It has no body, method override or credential header at the new call site; request rejects all other new paths and arbitrary headers. Existing ownership checks/internal-only network and finite HTTP/container deadlines remain.

Public asset verification requires HTTP 200 plus exact SHA-256 0f557a9f535a15acbe0fc7abb4fe896502a6d4c27de1c4145cfa001d0d2be099. Missing assets, HTML fallbacks and wrong bytes fail before readiness success, with owned runtime stopping in finally. Source extraction uses the fixed upstream asset path and matching checksum; Docker retains its pinned upstream image/source and corresponding-source/license packing.

The workflow retains contents: read, persist-credentials: false, push: false, no deployment environment or production credential input, bounded native fixture execution and retained failure evidence. No query annotation, query/category/threshold exclusion, plaintext encoding or alert dismissal is added.
residuals: Generated credentials remain plaintext during the real _FILE fixture, including existing Docker arguments/environments. Runner UID, host root and the local Docker daemon remain trusted; tmpfs may swap and abrupt failure may bypass cleanup.
A later Docker bind resolves a pathname. Same-UID/root substitution after verification and non-atomic cleanup against that actor are not eliminated.

This finite source review does not execute the fixture, establish native lifecycle behavior, clear any managed CodeQL alert, prove installed credential custody or authorize deployment. Exact-source tests, native qualification, managed scanner results and named-ref findings remain separate. An HTTP asset digest is not complete CAPTCHA or subscriber-journey acceptance.
expiry: Any change to the four pinned authority/caller sources or the bounded caller closure requires a fresh independent review; this witness is process evidence, not cryptographic approval.
